Basic Information for CVE-2025-70974 Vulnerability Information N/A Overview Fastjson versions prior to 1.2.48 contain a flaw in the handling of autoType. When a JSON document includes the @type key with a value specifying a Java class name, it may trigger invocation of public methods of that class, leading to security risks. Affected Versions Fastjson versions earlier than 1.2.48. Details The @type field is used to specify the target class for deserialization. When autoType is enabled, Fastjson instantiates the class specified by @type and may invoke its public methods. Attackers can craft malicious JSON payloads to exploit specific class methods, triggering JNDI injection. JNDI injection can load remote malicious code and execute arbitrary operations. This issue stems from an incomplete fix for CVE-2017-18349 and was further exploited via bypass techniques disclosed in CVE-2022-25845. Impact Can lead to Remote Code Execution (RCE). Has been actively exploited in real-world attacks between 2023 and 2025. Presents severe server-side security risks, especially in scenarios involving untrusted JSON input.
